BLOCKER: CTL-RLS-TENANT and CTL-TIMEOUT declare cwd=go/edpsvc but owner=edpdata / applies_to=go/edpdata/backlog.go; `go test ./...` in the edpsvc module never executes the edpdata fail-closed tests, so AC-3/AC-4 enforcement and its evidence are structurally unverifiable.
MAJOR: Rollback is stated twice and inconsistently: top-level `rollback` says "remove route, then 0019/0018 down" while `design_pack.rollback`/`rollback_recovery` include 0020; ambiguous recovery order is an operational hazard.
`requirements` restates AC-4 as "Missing migration 0016/0018" instead of AC-4's "0016-0020", silently dropping 0019/0020 from the fail-closed contract; the design contract and AC are out of sync.

Evidence artifacts required by controls and proof (`engineering/trails/BI-PF-1509-*.txt`, `BI-PF-1509-red.txt`) are not in `review_scope.files`/`affected_files`; the scope guard will flag them as stray paths or their evidence is out of scope — CL-010 and CL-016 enforcement contradict each other.
All five ACs share one identical evidence SHA (5adc48bf…), yet evidence spans Go svc tests, Go edpdata tests, and a Python guard; a single commit SHA cannot be current-run proof per AC (CL-010).

0020 index cleanup has no AC, no dedicated test reference, and no stated rationale beyond "in scope for rollback"; bundling an index drop into an admin-readiness item widens blast radius — prove the dropped index is not the access path for the tenant `item_count` query.

Counter recovery is under-specified: "interrupted apply = re-run" does not address a stale counter after partial apply/restore; no reconciliation-from-`backlog_id_reservations` step is defined for the restore-then-redeploy path.
MINOR: `failure_taxonomy` (8 reasons incl. conflict/exhausted, which this endpoint cannot emit) is wider than the pinned 5-label metric set; keep the metric label enum separately pinned to prevent cardinality drift.

`affected_components` includes `test-framework/tests` while the binding component list is [go/edpsvc, go/edpdata, migrations, ops, scripts]; align component allowlist with the scope guard or CI will reject declared paths.
Both transaction-local `statement_timeout=5s` and `PF_EDP_DB_TIMEOUT` bound Authority; document precedence so timeout classification (reason=timeout vs db_unavailable) is unambiguous.
Exact `count(backlog_items)` runs on every admin poll with no caching/ETag; poll frequency × large-tenant scan cost is unbounded beyond statement_timeout.
Single shared `PF_ADMIN_TOKEN` with constant-time compare is fine, but logs record `principal=admin` for all callers — no rotation/expiry or per-principal attribution for audit of an admin surface.
`api_contract` adds `Retry-After` on 503 while AC-4 mandates only a fixed safe message; pin the exact status/body/headers in a contract test to prevent drift.
CL-001 ownership is stated, but no `config/ownership.json` registration step is listed for the new route/metrics despite being referenced in `ownership`.
NIT: Alert expression `rate(...[10m]) > 0.05 for 5m` should state rate units and window semantics explicitly in the rules file.
`success_timestamp_seconds` gauge and `startup_ok` gauge partially overlap; name one as the alert source of truth in the runbook.
Failure matrix duplicates `failure_taxonomy`/`failure_matrix`/observability sections; consolidate to one source to avoid future divergence.
SUMMARY: Design is directionally sound: fail-closed 401/400/405/503, tenant-required queries, constant-time token compare, NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS evidence, bounded metrics, and a rehearsed rollback are all present.

Top risks: two enforced controls run against the wrong Go module (AC-3/AC-4 evidence invalid), a rollback order contradiction, and AC-contract drift on the migration fail-closed set (0016/0018 vs 0016-0020).
Resolve the control cwd/ownership mismatch, split evidence SHAs per AC, and reconcile scope-guard allowlist with evidence-trail paths before Gate 1.5.
